reason: The episode closed and edited several wayfinder tickets by hand. Each close touched the ticket frontmatter, a Resolution section, map.md Decisions so far, Not yet specified, and blocked_by lines. No existing skill covers this bookkeeping. The episode also added a research finding to Decisions so far before the user confirmed it, which design-question-rounds forbids. This skill states the close steps and that gate.
The factory could not see the rental-map folder. The trigger must also fire on that symptom so the next session loads the ticket format rules.

The episode showed the factory parser rejects frontmatter, three-digit names and lowercase labels. The format rules were only in a readback, so the close skill now carries them. The reader check is the proof step that caught the bad format.
The wayfinder command pointed at .wayfinder/map.md, which does not exist. The map is at .scratch/rental-map/map.md. The label line is the reliable way to find it, and this skill should say so.

A probe printed undefined for id and blockedBy, and the reply still said the reader worked. The skill should tell the next run to read the Ticket shape first and to treat undefined output as a failed check.

The filters ticket settled several domain terms and never updated the glossary. domain-modeling says to write terms down as they are resolved. This skill runs the ticket close, so it should carry that step.

In the episode the agent added an unconfirmed point (a listing added by hand has no link key, so only the maybe-match check runs) into the ticket Resolution as a fact-like line. The user had not confirmed it. The skill already says picks come from the user, but it does not say what to do with the agent's own inferences. This patch closes that gap.

The episode closed ticket 15 and created ticket 16 by chaining sed -i, cat >> or cat > and grep with && in one Bash call. The skill already requires one write per call, so the rule was not followed. Stating the chain case explicitly makes the rule concrete.

The new ticket 16 said the Apps Script research "found that ... a newer edit can still overwrite an older one". The ticket 10 Resolution in map.md records only the lock, text/plain POST, photo and id picks. The overwrite point was the agent's own inference, written as a research finding, and the reply did not ask about it.

The episode added a Spec pointer and two new open questions to map.md without loading this skill, which covers map.md edits. The rule for where a document pointer goes was not followed by reading this skill first.

Tickets for the build of the rental map were written to a second folder, .scratch/rental-map-build/issues. The same header rules apply there, but the skill only names the first folder, so a later session may miss the header format.
